app.title: Thousands of Lives
app.tagline: One life in a random era of human history. Learn, survive, shape your fate and decide whether your family line goes on.
beta.notice: This is a beta. The historical texts were prepared with the help of AI and have not yet been checked by a historian. Only one era is available for now, Antiquity; more are coming.
setup.title: New life

setup.mortality.soft.desc: Children die less often than they really did
setup.mortality.historical.desc: As in the sources: almost a third of children died before age one

setup.warning: The game includes disease, war, slavery and death. They are described without graphic detail. Ages 15+.

about.title: About the data and sources
about.body1: Thousands of Lives simulates a single human life in the past. We try to make events, occupations, laws and risks fit the era, but the game is a simplification.
about.body2: Mortality in Antiquity is based on the Coale–Demeny model life tables (West, around level 3), which historians use for the Roman Empire. Life expectancy at birth was about 25 years, mostly because of high child mortality. This is a reconstruction, not precise data.
about.body3: Every historian's note is marked "confirmed by sources", "reconstruction" or "disputed".
about.beta: The beta texts were prepared with the help of AI and have not yet been checked by a historian. If you spot a mistake, let us know.
about.source.1: Coale A., Demeny P. Regional Model Life Tables and Stable Populations. 2nd ed. 1983.
about.source.2: Bagnall R., Frier B. The Demography of Roman Egypt. Cambridge, 1994.
about.source.3: Scheidel W. (ed.) The Cambridge Companion to the Roman Economy. 2012.
about.source.4: Thucydides. History of the Peloponnesian War (on the war and the plague of Athens).
about.source.5: Polybius, Livy, Plutarch, Suetonius on events of Roman history.
about.privacy: Saves are stored only in your browser. Yandex Metrica is used for visit statistics.
